claims.text: Add doc comment explaining TxMiss is used both when txid is missing and when the block is pruned, and clarify redundant phrasing
claims.quote: This struct is used both when a TXID is not found in the index, and when it is found, but the block is not found (pruned). This could be mentioned in a doc comment on the struct.
claims.status_note: reviewer recognized distinction cannot be made due to prefix false positives
claims.status_by_quote: I would've argued for a stronger conceptual distinction between "Not in the index" and the "In the index but in a pruned node", but I have realized, that, due to the potential prefix false positives, this is in fact not possible.

claims.text: Separate the 3 lookup cases (found, found in pruned block, not found) in comments/code for clarity
claims.quote: For clarity it would be better to separate 3 cases: found, found in pruned block, and not found at all in the index.
claims.status_note: reviewer recognized distinction cannot be made due to prefix false positives
claims.status_by_quote: Same as above: I would've argued for a stronger conceptual distinction between "Not in the index" and the "In the index but in a pruned node", but I have realized, that, due to the potential prefix false positives, this is in fact not possible.

claims.text: Update REST documentation to clarify that a block may not have been indexed or has been pruned
claims.quote: What about if it exists in a block that was not indexed? More correct would be "in a block that has not been indexed or that has been pruned"
claims.status_note: author adopted the suggested documentation wording

support.reason: no reason given: Big concept ACK :D/
I think expected block usage is about 100GB per year, so 5 years worth of history would be half a terabyte, and probably cover most lookups... Concept ACK, looks okay to me at first glance.
I'm excited about this PR and I love the idea and the approach... we can even access txs on pruned nodes, since #35531 the index stores the block 'virtual' reference rather than a file position
The ability to have a txindex holding information of _all_ transactions even in case of a pruned node is a huge improvement, it makes pruned nodes much more capable.
